name: Marco Zhang

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. What does an ordinary day at your accounting firm involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The independent cinema sends its ticket takings with a second list of cancelled shows, and I check the refunds before preparing its accounts and tax return. I have done this work long enough to know where a missing ticket hides, and I like explaining a clean figure to the owner; I dread the box of unsigned refund slips that arrives on filing day. I am 58, with a bachelor's degree and a professional accountancy qualification, and I am an experienced mid-level accountant rather than a team lead. I have never used AI at work; the signed slip and bank statement are my starting point.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI remains small, a sorter might move the slips into date order, but the cancellation still needs a bank check. I would carry on with the same signed return process.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the cinema to keep each refund slip with the ticket report. I would tell colleagues not to call a sorted pile a checked account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My wage is on the low side for an accountant, and my partner Farah and I have less than a month of expenses saved. Our grown children have their own rent, our current rent and bills take most of two wages, and there are few comparable firms nearby; that makes a quiet year tight.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the paid cinema returns and asking for missing signed refunds before filing. I would stop the paid film-streaming plan at renewal and transfer its monthly charge into cash only after our rent, food and travel are paid from actual wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the bills we have now. A machine that mostly disappoints cannot fix a thin household account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why cancel films when the cinema is your client?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The home subscription is separate from the cinema's work. I can still watch a film now and then without paying for an unused plan every month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What about retirement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I hope it comes within reach, but I do not know what income I could rely on yet. I will not count a date as money for rent.

say: I would keep **signed refund slips** with each ticket report.
I would call a **sorted pile** different from a checked account.
think: Our **low wage** and under-one-month reserve already strain rent and food.
Few local firms limit my **replacement work** even in a mild AI world.
do: Keep **paid cinema returns** and obtain signed refunds before filing.
Cancel **film streaming** and deposit its charge only after rent, food and travel are paid.
feel: I feel **anxious** about existing household bills.
S0.quote: A machine that mostly disappoints cannot fix a thin household account.
fieldNote: His experience gives him a **reliable refund check**, but low pay and almost no savings drive baseline anxiety.
The streaming cancellation creates **new cash** only if actual wages first cover rent, food and travel.

steps.text: Keep paid cinema returns and obtain signed refund slips before filing
Cancel streaming and deposit its charge only after rent food and travel

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing the return and checking ticket refunds are thinking tasks, so my desk would change before robots reach the cinema floor. I can see the firm asking one reviewer to cover more clients.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the staff union to demand written notice before anyone loses paid hours. I would tell the cinema owner someone must answer if a refund is missed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the firm to cut a large part of my checking week as software handles the basic slips. Farah's school-catering wage varies by term, and with less than a month saved a lost day would take rent money; I have been lying awake over that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would join the staff union's request for written hour-cut notice and keep the paid cinema files still assigned. I would take the firm's required AI walkthrough only if the requirement is in writing and it is supervised on paid time; if not, I would keep the authorised manual check while work is offered. If my hours fall in the first year, I would take a posted accounts job only with written pay, hours and start date covering rent and the bus after fares.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect a big cut to my wage. I can look at a required screen, but I cannot pay rent with a trial certificate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you put a live cinema file into the tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, not without the firm's written approval after a paid trial on old files. I have never used AI and will not guess on a client's tax return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the union cannot prevent cuts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would still want the written last-paid-day notice and keep any shifts offered. A union cannot invent a vacancy, but it can make the timing clear.

say: I would seek **written hour-cut notice** through the union.
I would keep a **named refund answerer** for the cinema.
think: I expect a **large cut** to my paid checking week.
Farah's variable wage cannot cover **rent** if my shifts fall.
do: Join the **union request** for written notice and keep assigned paid files while offered.
Take a **required AI walkthrough** only with written requirement and paid supervision; use live only after paid old-file trial and written approval.
After cuts take a **posted accounts job** only with written after-fare rent-covering pay, hours and start.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about a likely large wage cut.
S1.quote: I can look at a required screen, but I cannot pay rent with a trial certificate.
fieldNote: He has never used AI and accepts only **required, paid supervision**, not a private experiment on live client returns.
Written notice and a posted replacement with **after-fare rent-covering wages** are separate practical responses.

steps.text: Join union request for written notice and keep offered paid files
Take written-required AI walkthrough only on paid supervised time; otherwise retain authorised manual checks
Use live cinema files only after paid old-file trial and written firm approval
After cuts take posted accounts job with written after-fare rent-covering pay hours start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could judge the refund and finish the cinema return without me. Robots around 2031 might later clean a theatre, but the tax desk would be exposed first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the union to demand severance and last-paid-shift dates in writing. I would tell the cinema owner to keep original ticket records even if the firm changes its software.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my accounting post to end when AGI can do the whole filing job cheaply. Our savings would last weeks and Farah's wage alone will not cover rent; I wake at night counting those weeks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask the union for written severance and keep every paid return offered until the firm ends the post. If it ends in the first year after 2028, I would use the small reserve for rent and food while applying to posted cinema box-office clerk roles, taking one only with written wage, hours and start date covering rent after bus fares. Ticket booking is thinking work too, so I would take an actual paid opening as a bridge, not safety from AGI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed by the expected loss of my wage. I know the cinema well, but its familiarity is not a job offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Farah take extra shifts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the school confirms them. I will not fill a rent budget with catering hours that have not been put on a rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no box-office vacancy appears?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep paid firm files while offered, then contact the landlord before a missed payment if the post ends without an offer. I would not assume the cinema can hire me.

say: I would demand **written severance** and last-paid-shift dates.
I would keep **original ticket records** through a software change.
think: I expect my **accounting post** to end in 2028.
Our **weeks of savings** and Farah's wage cannot cover a long rent gap.
do: Ask the **union** for severance and keep paid returns only while offered.
Use **reserve for bills** after loss; contact landlord before a threatened missed rent payment if no offer exists.
Take a **posted cinema job** only with written after-fare rent-covering wage, hours and start.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by likely loss of rent-paying work.
S2.quote: I know the cinema well, but its familiarity is not a job offer.
fieldNote: The **2028 accounting desk loss** comes before capable robots affect physical theatre work; box-office booking remains exposed.
He counts **paid files** only while offered, then uses the small reserve and seeks an actually posted bridge.

steps.text: Ask union for written severance and keep offered paid returns until actual end
After loss use reserve; take posted cinema job with written after-fare rent-covering wage hours start
Contact landlord before missed rent if post ends without offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years lets me find out whether a cinema will still pay a person to resolve ticket disputes after AGI reaches accounts in 2031. Robots around 2034 are later for physical work in the building.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm and union for a posted, paid refunds role rather than a vague course invitation. I would tell colleagues that a promised title is no replacement for wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Routine tax preparation may lose its fee, but I have handled cancelled-show disputes for years. I could take assigned paid calls without pretending I am a new technology expert.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would handle one ticket-refund call each month only if the firm assigns it on paid time and a supervisor checks the answer. I would keep paid returns while offered and take a posted refunds-clerk role before or after 2031 only with written wage, hours and start date covering rent after bus fare. If the return work ends first, I would use the reserve for bills during the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the tax wage, but five years lets me test whether anyone budgets for the calls. An unpaid phone call is not a new post.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you study another course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if a real posted role requires it and the employer pays the fee and study hours. Otherwise I will use the free refund guidance and keep paid work available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks the call?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My supervisor Dev would listen to the first answer and sign the note before it goes to the cinema. I know the refunds, but I still want a second ear on a disputed tax amount.

say: I would seek a **posted paid refunds role** rather than count a vague course invitation as income.
I would reject a **promised title** without wages.
think: My cancelled-show experience might support **paid calls** if someone budgets them.
do: Handle **one refund call monthly** only with Dev-assigned paid supervision; otherwise keep paid returns.
Use **free refund guidance**; take a required course only for posted paid work with funded fees and paid study hours.
Take a **posted refunds job** only with written after-fare rent-covering wage, hours and start; after loss use reserve.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the future tax wage.
S3.quote: An unpaid phone call is not a new post.
fieldNote: His current experience is in **cinema refunds**, and the new call must be assigned and checked on paid time.
A course needs **posted work** and funded paid study; free guidance and current paid files remain fallback.

steps.text: Keep paid returns and free guidance; handle monthly refund call only with Dev-assigned paid supervision
Take required course only for posted paid role with funded fees and paid study hours
Use reserve after loss; take posted refunds job anytime with written after-fare rent-covering wage hours start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years puts me at 68 when AGI reaches the tax desk in 2036. Robots around 2039 are later for cleaning and other physical cinema work, but I cannot assume this accounts post lasts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm for a written staffing timeline and the retirement provider for an income statement. I would tell Farah we must check the rent against actual numbers before setting a date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would like to leave full-time work sometime, but I do not know what income would replace my low wage. Our savings are under a month, so I cannot treat a hoped-for retirement date as a way to pay rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would get a written retirement-income statement and compare it with a year of our actual rent, food and travel costs before choosing any date. I would keep taking paid cinema returns while offered; if the post ends in the first year after 2036 and the figures do not cover costs, I would use the reserve for bills and take a posted clerk job only with written wage, hours and start date covering rent after travel. I would keep working if the statement is not enough, not assume an age gives me an income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about today's bills despite the longer timetable. A full year of costs may show we need the wage longer than I hoped.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would grown children cover a gap?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, our grown children have their own rent and food to buy. I would ask them to read a confusing statement, not finance our decision.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the firm proposes fewer hours before 2036?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would accept only a written paid schedule if its wage plus any verified retirement income covers the year's costs. Otherwise I would keep the paid hours offered and look at posted roles if they end.

say: I would seek **written figures** for staffing and income before setting a date.
I would check **rent and food** against a full year's costs.
think: I do not know what retirement income would **replace my wage**.
Our **thin savings** cannot cover an unsupported decision to stop work.
do: Request a **written income statement** and yearly bills; reduce hours only with written rota and verified income covering costs.
Keep **paid cinema returns** while offered; after loss use reserve if income falls short.
After 2036 loss and income shortfall, take a **posted clerk job** only with written after-travel rent-covering wage, hours and start.
feel: I feel **anxious** about current bills and unknown later income.
S4.quote: A full year of costs may show we need the wage longer than I hoped.
fieldNote: He checks a **written income statement** against full-year costs before any reduced-hours or stop-work choice.
No retirement entitlement is assumed; paid files count **only while offered**, and a later job needs posted written terms.

steps.text: Request written income and yearly costs; reduce hours only with written rota and enough income
Keep paid cinema returns while offered; after loss use reserve if income short
After 2036 loss and shortfall take posted clerk job with written after-travel rent-covering wage hours start

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I could lose my low-paid but necessary accounting post before we have a month of bills saved. Written severance, notice of the last paid shift and a real posted wage that covers rent would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who will explain the cancelled-show refund when a client disputes the tax figure. I have spent enough evenings finding signed cinema refunds to know why disputed tax figures matter.

headlineQuote: I have spent enough evenings finding signed cinema refunds to know why disputed tax figures matter.
portrait: Marco is a **58-year-old experienced mid-level accountant** with a bachelor's degree and professional qualification.
His **low pay**, under-one-month reserve and few local firms make ordinary bills worrying.
He **never uses AI**, wants paid required instruction, and asks the union for notice.
He tests **paid refund calls** while treating retirement as a decision that needs written income figures.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** scenario could end his necessary wage before even one month of savings exists.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written severance and notice**, plus a posted rent-covering job.
